statement: For a lowercase byte c let val(c) = code(c) - 97. For lowercase bytes c,d let dist(c,d) = min(|val(c)-val(d)|, 26 - |val(c)-val(d)|). For an integer L with 1 <= L <= len(s) and indices i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_{L-1} in [0,len(s)), define pcost(i_0,...,i_{L-1}) = sum_{t=0}^{floor(L/2)-1} dist(s[i_t], s[i_{L-1-t}]). The function returns a result r, and r is the largest such L for which there exist indices i_0 < ... < i_{L-1} satisfying pcost(i_0,...,i_{L-1}) <= k.
preconditions: s is a slice of bytes with 1 <= len(s) <= 200, k is an i64 with 1 <= k <= 200, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), s[i] is an ASCII lowercase letter ('a'..'z', codes 97..122).
